For this node, strongest evidence categories to survive later layers are product-line mapping, customer/OEM qualification, lead times, capacity additions, revenue attribution, and margin sensitivity in force-torque sensors, encoders, servo drives, machine vision, and NdFeB magnets.

VPG should be tracked as an underfollowed US-listed precision force/strain sensor candidate for robotics; key survival test is whether humanoid orders become material production revenue rather than prototype activity.

ALNT should be tracked as an underfollowed US-listed motion-control and actuation subsystem candidate; key survival test is proof of qualified robotics sockets, especially motors, drives, gearheads, encoders, or integrated actuator modules.
CGNX is a machine-vision reference anchor, not the primary alpha-hunt target; use it to benchmark automation/vision demand and market attention against smaller suppliers.
